LUREX: Lunar Radiation Environment Explorer
MAE 342 · Spacecraft Design · Team of 16
Propulsion · Launch Vehicle
Propulsion & Launch Vehicle poster with team
Propulsion module CAD: hydrazine and MON-3 layout

Led propulsion and launch vehicle systems engineering for a two-satellite lunar mission (MiLO and LiLO) designed to characterize the lunar radiation environment from low and mid lunar orbit. Built the formal requirements, delta-V budget, and thruster trade study that drove the propulsion architecture. Led a propulsion and launch vehicle subteam of four.

Selected a shared hydrazine tank feeding both a MON-3 main engine and eight monopropellant RCS thrusters to minimize failure points, then sized propellant load, tank volume, and wet mass against ESPA Grande secondary-payload constraints.

Megatron: Autonomous Search & Rescue Robot
Mechanical Design Course · Team Lead, Team of 10
Mechanical Systems
Completed chassis: large-wheel drivetrain and arm
Cleated wheel: the wall-breaching mechanism

Owned the chassis and drivetrain for a large-wheel autonomous robot built to navigate a simulated disaster course and deliver a medical kit to a trapped victim. The signature mechanism (oversized cleated wheels that also serve as the wall-breaching method) came from a free-body analysis of the torque needed to climb a 6-inch breach wall, setting wheel radius and motor sizing.

Coordinated integration across mechanical, electrical, and software teams through final delivery. The robot was the only one in the course to complete the full course autonomously.

Weight38.6 lb (50 lb max)
Course time~1:00 (5:00 max)
Top speed~2.8 mph

Wing Design and Build Project
MAE Lab · Structural Design & Testing · Team Project
CAD · FEA · Fabrication
Aftermath of 180 lb destructive test: failure at predicted location
Final beam FEA with lightening holes (Siemens NX / ANSYS)

Designed, analyzed, and fabricated an aluminum wing section with an internal spar and rib structure. Used Siemens NX and ANSYS FEA to optimize spar geometry with lightening holes, meeting the load requirement at minimum weight. Built the wing in the MAE shop (milling, drilling, fastener assembly) and load-tested to destruction at 180 lbs; failure at the predicted location validated the FEA model.

Weightrack: Home Gym Weight Rack
MAE Shop · Mechanical Design & FEA · Solo Project
CAD · Fabrication
Final assembly CAD: A-frame with welds, plates, and barbell cradle
Strain analysis: max principal strain under 295 lb full load

Designed and analyzed a steel weight rack holding 15 Olympic plates (295 lbs) across four adjustable pegs. A-frame uses 1×2" 4130 chromoly steel tubing, 1144 carbon steel rod stock for lathe-turned pegs and barbell cradle, and a 2×3" stainless steel bridge at the top. Design prioritized manufacturability (standardized tubing, consistent weld joints) and multifunctionality. FEA confirmed the structure is well within elastic limits: max stress ~10,000 psi (13% of yield), max deflection 0.017" at peg tips.

Alternative Propellants for Hall Effect Thrusters
MAE 426 · Research Presentation · Team of 5
Electric Propulsion
Published HET performance data: xenon vs. solid iodine propellant
HET with inclined inward plume divergence

A research presentation synthesizing published studies on solid iodine as a low-cost alternative to xenon and argon for Hall effect thrusters, framed as a response to SpaceX's switch to argon in Starlink V2 Mini. Iodine's atomic mass and ionization energy closely track xenon's, while its solid storage at 3x the density of pressurized xenon and ~$30/kg cost make it attractive for constellation-scale deployment.

Also reviewed published findings on how inward-inclined magnetic topology and combined radial-propellant injection reduce plume divergence and improve specific impulse in next-generation thrusters.

Propellant studyIodine vs. Xe / Ar
Iodine cost~$30/kg
Density gain3x vs. pressurized Xe
Isp similarityClose match to Xe
Plume focusInward inclined topology

Shepard: Mars Sojourner Recovery Trajectory
MAE 341 · Spaceflight Dynamics · STK Astrogator
Orbital Mechanics
Full interplanetary trajectory: STK Astrogator output

Designed a full interplanetary mission concept in STK to recover NASA's long-dormant Sojourner rover from Mars and return it to Earth. Built Earth-to-Mars and Mars-to-Earth transfer arcs with Lambert solvers, a Mars parking orbit inclined to repeatedly overfly the Ares Vallis landing site, and a 16-month hold in Mars orbit timed to the next return launch window.

Worked through real STK constraints (propagator accuracy versus runtime, differential-corrector convergence for orbit insertion and inclination changes) that mirror the trade-offs mission designers face when building real trajectory solutions.

Total delta-V22.6 km/s
Mars stay16 months
ToolSTK Astrogator
MethodLambert solvers
Target siteAres Vallis
